node.title: Re^2: Creating data delimited by ASCII code 1 using perl (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
TIMTOWTDI Party? ;-)

print "\x{0001}"; print "\N{U+1}"; print "\N{START OF HEADING}"; print chr(1); print v1; print "x"^"y"; vec(my $x,0,8)=1; print $x;

Update: "x"^"y" only works if the new [doc://feature#The-'bitwise'-feature|bitwise feature] is off; it could be turned on implicitly by the -E switch or a use 5.028; or higher (thanks for pointing this out, [davido]!). When the bitwise feature is on, one has to use the new ^. operator instead. Also, \N{START OF HEADING} requires [doc://charnames] to be loaded explicitly on Perls before 5.16.
